_purpose: D4 — Translator-Network Capacity probe. Train translator MLPs T:zA→zB at depths {1,2,4,8} with 5 seeds each per direction (A→B and B→A); the minimal depth at which val_mse_rel < 0.10 quantifies cross-pathway structural distance. Drives the decide-phase mechanism label alongside D1+D2+D3.
_notes: Hyperparameters of the underlying §5.7 baseline (ssl_epochs, ft_epochs, ft_lr, n_seeds_per_config, n_eval_seeds, lambda_c) intentionally identical to D1/D2/D3 so the (zA, zB) substrate is byte-equivalent across all four diagnostics.

Translator MLP per spec methods/D4-translator-capacity.md: depth-d means d Linear layers with ReLU between (depth=1 is pure Linear). Hidden=64 throughout. Loss = mean per-row squared error against cosine-normalized target z_B/||z_B||. val_mse_rel = mean per-row ||T(z_A)-z_B_unit||^2 (||z_B_unit||^2=1 by construction so this is the relative residual).

Training: full-batch Adam (lr=1e-3, b1=0.9, b2=0.999, eps=1e-8), translator_steps=600 (≈ spec's 200 epochs × 3 effective full-batch steps for n_train≈432), early-stop on val loss with patience=80 steps (no improvement). Spec's mini-batch=64 collapsed to full-batch for JIT simplicity; n_train≈432 fits trivially in L40S memory and total ops <1e7 per fit.
5 seeds per (depth, direction): vary translator init only (data split is fixed across seeds). 5 PASS verdicts averaged; depth PASSes if mean val_mse_rel < 0.10.
Pass threshold per spec: val_mse_rel < 0.10 = T reconstructs target to within 10% squared-error relative to unit-norm target (linear-scale) — the spec's 'low residual' criterion.
Direction asymmetry recorded: spec notes A→B converging at depth 2 while B→A needs depth 8 (or vice versa) reveals which pathway carries more reconstruction-only-from-the-other information.
Diagnosis routing per spec table: min_capacity=1 (linear) → basis-ambiguity; =2 → mild-nonlinear; =4 → heavy-nonlinear; =8 or none-converging → information-mismatch.
Per-depth params and wall_s recorded for the reviewer-facing scaling curve (spec calls this out explicitly).
